accepted.s: UDAY, introduced in November 2015, is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Financial turnaround of state-owned electricity distribution companies
Universal installation of solar pumps in rural areas
Construction of nuclear power plants by state governments
Replacement of LPG with electric cooking appliances
accepted.x: UDAY, or Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana, was introduced by the Ministry of Power in November 2015 for the financial turnaround of state discoms.
accepted.tq: Identify the scheme from its ministry, year and core purpose.
accepted.sec: UDAY - discom debt takeover, share covered, states, outcomes

accepted.s: Under the UDAY debt restructuring arrangement, what proportion of the discom debt was to be taken over by the states through state bonds?
accepted.x: States took over 75% of discom debt outstanding as on 30 September 2015 through state bonds.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the debt-takeover share from the separate percentage of total debt covered by participating states.
accepted.sec: UDAY - discom debt takeover, share covered, states, outcomes

accepted.s: The 75% takeover of discom debt under UDAY was structured in which manner?
accepted.x: The states were to take over 50% of the debt in 2015-16 and the remaining 25% in 2016-17.
accepted.tq: Break a total figure into its year-wise components.
accepted.sec: UDAY - discom debt takeover, share covered, states, outcomes

accepted.s:
Which of the following were targets under UDAY for 2018-19?
1. Reduction of AT&C losses to 15%
2. Elimination of the ACS-ARR gap
3. Reduction of rooftop solar installations to zero

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: UDAY targeted AT&C losses of 15% and an ACS-ARR gap of zero by 2018-19. Rooftop solar installations were not a UDAY target.
accepted.tq: Find the statement belonging to another energy programme.
accepted.sec: UDAY - discom debt takeover, share covered, states, outcomes

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reported change in AT&C losses under UDAY-related outcomes?
o: 22.62% in FY14 to zero in FY25
accepted.x: Reported AT&C losses declined from 22.62% in FY14 to 15.04% in FY25.
accepted.tq: Read the direction and endpoints of a time-based comparison carefully.
accepted.sec: UDAY - discom debt takeover, share covered, states, outcomes

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the power-sector outcomes associated with UDAY:
1. The demand-supply gap was 4.2% in FY14.
2. The demand-supply gap became zero in November 2025.
3. The AT&C loss was 15.04% in FY25.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the demand-supply gap fell from 4.2% in FY14 to zero in November 2025, while AT&C losses were 15.04% in FY25.
accepted.tq: Combine two related trend comparisons without reversing their time sequence.
accepted.sec: UDAY - discom debt takeover, share covered, states, outcomes

accepted.s: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana was launched in February 2024 by which ministry as a Central Sector Scheme?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: The scheme was launched in February 2024 by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy as a Central Sector Scheme.
accepted.tq: Use the ministry-scheme association as the decisive clue.
accepted.sec: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana - free units, subsidy, household target

accepted.s: The approved outlay of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana is:
accepted.x: The outlay of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana is ₹75,021 crore.
accepted.tq: Separate the scheme outlay from the RDSS outlay and grant figures.
accepted.sec: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana - free units, subsidy, household target

accepted.s: What is the household target of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana by March 2027?
accepted.x: The scheme targets rooftop solar installations in 1 crore households by FY 2026-27, that is, March 2027.
accepted.tq: Match the target number with the stated completion year.
accepted.sec: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana - free units, subsidy, household target

accepted.s: Under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, households may receive free electricity up to:
accepted.x: The scheme provides for free power of up to 300 units per month, with beneficiary households becoming prosumers.
accepted.tq: Test the exact monthly ceiling rather than the broader rooftop-solar objective.
accepted.sec: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana - free units, subsidy, household target

accepted.s: Under the Central Financial Assistance structure of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, which statement is correct?
o: 40% of the cost is covered for 2 kW and 60% for additional capacity up to 3 kW.
100% of the cost is covered up to 3 kW.
30% of the cost is covered for 2 kW and 30% for additional capacity up to 3 kW.
60% of the cost is covered for 2 kW and 40% for additional capacity up to 3 kW.
accepted.x: CFA covers 60% of the cost for 2 kW and 40% for the additional capacity up to 3 kW.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the two subsidy percentages and their capacity limits.
accepted.sec: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana - free units, subsidy, household target

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana:
1. It aims at 30 GW of rooftop solar capacity.
2. It targets saving 1,000 billion units of power over 25 years.
3. It aims to reduce 720 million tonnes of carbon dioxide over 25 years.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The scheme’s stated long-term goals include 30 GW of rooftop solar, 1,000 BU of power savings and a 720 MT reduction in CO2 over 25 years.
accepted.tq: Check whether all quantitative goals belong to the same scheme.
accepted.sec: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana - free units, subsidy, household target

accepted.s: Under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, which institutional arrangement is envisaged for districts?
o: One Model Solar Village per district
One solar pump in every village
Two nuclear villages in every district
accepted.x: The scheme provides for one Model Solar Village per district.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact unit of implementation and its numerical provision.
accepted.sec: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana - free units, subsidy, household target

accepted.s: The City Accelerator Programme associated with PM Surya Ghar was launched primarily to provide technical assistance to:
o: Farmers and irrigation departments for solar pumps
ULBs and discoms for urban rooftop solar
LPG distributors for rural refill delivery
Nuclear power corporations for reactor construction
accepted.x: The City Accelerator Programme, launched in June 2025, provides technical help to urban local bodies and discoms for urban rooftop solar.
accepted.tq: Match the programme’s beneficiaries with its specific implementation problem.
accepted.sec: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana - free units, subsidy, household target

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the progress reported for PM Surya Ghar during 1 January–22 December 2025?
o: 18.14 lakh rooftop solar systems and 14.43 lakh households
14.43 lakh rooftop solar systems and 18.14 lakh households
30 lakh rooftop solar systems and 1 crore households
1.443 lakh rooftop solar systems and 1.814 lakh households
accepted.x: The reported progress was 14.43 lakh rooftop solar systems covering 18.14 lakh households during the stated period.
accepted.tq: Keep installations and beneficiary households in their correct order and units.
accepted.sec: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana - free units, subsidy, household target

accepted.s: How many willing households were electrified under Saubhagya according to the latest reported figure?
accepted.x: Saubhagya electrified 2.86 crore willing households. An older figure cited 2.82 crore households as of March 2021.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the updated figure from the older reference figure.
accepted.sec: Saubhagya - launch, target, completion

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the households covered by the ₹6,521 crore sanctioned under RDSS for Saubhagya leftovers?
o: 9.42 lakh farming households with solar pumps
13.65 lakh households, including specified vulnerable and difficult-area groups
1 crore urban households with rooftop solar
accepted.x: ₹6,521 crore was sanctioned for 13.65 lakh leftover households, including PVTGs under PM-JANMAN, tribal households under DAJGUA, SC households under PMAJAY and border villages under Vibrant Villages.
accepted.tq: Match the amount and beneficiary count before checking the special categories.
accepted.sec: Saubhagya - launch, target, completion

accepted.s: DDUGJY was conveyed by the Ministry of Power on 3 December 2014 and replaced which earlier programme?
accepted.x: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana was conveyed on 3 December 2014 and replaced the Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana (RGGVY).
accepted.tq: Use the predecessor-programme relationship to separate rural and urban schemes.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY - feeder separation, village electrification milestone

accepted.s: Which organisation served as the nodal agency for DDUGJY?
accepted.x: Rural Electrification Corporation (REC) was the nodal agency for DDUGJY.
accepted.tq: Identify the implementing agency rather than the ministry responsible for the scheme.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY - feeder separation, village electrification milestone

accepted.s: The principal goal of DDUGJY was to provide:
o: 300 free units per month to rooftop-solar households
Urban smart meters in all municipal wards
Deposit-free LPG connections to poor women
accepted.x: DDUGJY sought to provide 24×7 power for rural India through rural distribution strengthening and electrification measures.
accepted.tq: Link the scheme to its stated sectoral and geographical goal.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY - feeder separation, village electrification milestone

accepted.s:
Which of the following were components of DDUGJY?
1. Separation of agricultural and non-agricultural feeders
2. Sub-transmission strengthening
3. Micro/off-grid networks and metering
4. Rural electrification

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four listed measures were components of DDUGJY.
accepted.tq: Check whether the listed infrastructure measures form one integrated scheme.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY - feeder separation, village electrification milestone

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I
(a) Date of electrification milestone
(b) Number of inhabited census villages electrified
(c) Last village electrified
(d) State of the last village

List-II
(i) Manipur
(ii) 28 April 2018
(iii) Leisang
(iv) 18,374
accepted.x: The milestone occurred on 28 April 2018; 18,374 inhabited census villages were electrified; the last village was Leisang in Manipur.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure date-place pair and eliminate incompatible codes.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY - feeder separation, village electrification milestone

accepted.s: The village electrification milestone achieved under DDUGJY was described by the IEA as:
o: The largest urban distribution reform in India
One of the world's greatest success stories
The first nuclear electrification project in Asia
accepted.x: The International Energy Agency described the electrification of all inhabited census villages as one of the world's greatest success stories.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive external assessment associated with the milestone.
accepted.sec: DDUGJY - feeder separation, village electrification milestone

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS):
1. It was approved in 2021.
2. Its approved outlay was ₹3,03,758 crore.
3. Its Gross Budgetary Support was ₹97,631 crore.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: RDSS was approved in 2021 with an outlay of ₹3,03,758 crore, including Gross Budgetary Support of ₹97,631 crore.
accepted.tq: Test the year, total outlay and budgetary-support figure together.
accepted.sec: RDSS - smart meters, loss-reduction targets, outlay

accepted.s: The national targets of RDSS include:
o: AT&C losses of 12–15% and an ACS-ARR gap of zero
AT&C losses of zero and an ACS-ARR gap of 12–15%
AT&C losses of 30% and an ACS-ARR gap of 15%
Only reduction of transmission losses, without an ACS-ARR target
accepted.x: RDSS aims at pan-India AT&C losses of 12–15% and an ACS-ARR gap of zero.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the two performance indicators and their target values.
accepted.sec: RDSS - smart meters, loss-reduction targets, outlay

accepted.s: Which of the following is a principal intervention under RDSS?
o: Prepaid smart metering and loss-reduction works
Replacement of all agricultural feeders by rooftop solar
Free LPG refills and improved stove design
accepted.x: RDSS focuses on prepaid smart metering and works for reducing distribution losses.
accepted.tq: Match the operational intervention with the distribution-sector reform scheme.
accepted.sec: RDSS - smart meters, loss-reduction targets, outlay

accepted.s: Which component of PM-KUSUM relates to decentralised grid-connected solar or renewable-energy plants on farm or barren land?
accepted.x: Component A provides for decentralised grid-connected solar or renewable-energy plants on farm or barren land.
accepted.tq: Match the component letter with its specific intervention.
accepted.sec: PM-KUSUM - components A, B, C; subsidy sharing

accepted.s: Under PM-KUSUM, Component B and Component C respectively refer to:
o: Solarisation of grid-connected pumps; standalone solar pumps
Urban rooftop solar; prepaid smart meters
Standalone solar pumps; solarisation of grid-connected pumps
Farm solar plants; rural feeder separation
accepted.x: Component B covers standalone solar pumps, while Component C covers solarisation of grid-connected pumps.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two closely related pump components.
accepted.sec: PM-KUSUM - components A, B, C; subsidy sharing

accepted.s: PM-KUSUM was launched in 2019 by which ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
accepted.x: PM-KUSUM was launched in 2019 by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
accepted.tq: Use the ministry and launch year to separate PM-KUSUM from other rural schemes.
accepted.sec: PM-KUSUM - components A, B, C; subsidy sharing

accepted.s: For Components B and C of PM-KUSUM, the subsidy-sharing pattern is:
accepted.x: For Components B and C, the Centre contributes 30%, the State 30% and the farmer 40%; a bank loan may also be used by the farmer.
accepted.tq: Check the three-way percentage split without confusing it with rooftop-solar CFA.
accepted.sec: PM-KUSUM - components A, B, C; subsidy sharing

accepted.s: Decentralised solarisation under PM-KUSUM provides daytime irrigation and additional income to approximately how many farmers?
accepted.x: Decentralised solarisation provides daytime irrigation and extra income to over 21.77 lakh farmers.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the farmer-beneficiary count from the pump-installation counts.
accepted.sec: PM-KUSUM - components A, B, C; subsidy sharing

accepted.s: The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana was launched in 2016 by the:
o: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
accepted.x: PMUY was launched in 2016 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to provide deposit-free LPG connections to poor women.
accepted.tq: Match the clean-cooking scheme with its administrative ministry.
accepted.sec: Clean cooking access - PM Ujjwala Yojana, refill issues

accepted.s: What was the Phase I target of PMUY by 2019?
accepted.x: Phase I of PMUY targeted 8 crore deposit-free LPG connections by 2019; the reported number of connections later exceeded 9.5 crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original target from the later cumulative achievement.
accepted.sec: Clean cooking access - PM Ujjwala Yojana, refill issues

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with Ujjwala 2.0?
o: Free first refill and stove, self-declaration facility for migrants, and ₹1,600 assistance per 14.2 kg connection
Free electricity up to 300 units and 60% rooftop-solar subsidy
A ₹6,521 crore package for border villages only
accepted.x: Ujjwala 2.0 provides a free first refill and stove, permits migrants to use self-declaration, and provides cash assistance of ₹1,600 per 14.2 kg connection.
accepted.tq: Group several features belonging to one phase instead of mixing schemes.
accepted.sec: Clean cooking access - PM Ujjwala Yojana, refill issues

accepted.s: Since October 2023, the targeted subsidy for PMUY beneficiaries has been:
o: ₹200 per 14.2 kg refill for up to 12 refills a year
₹300 per 5 kg refill without an annual limit
₹1,600 per 14.2 kg refill for up to 5 refills a year
₹300 per 14.2 kg refill for up to 9 refills a year
accepted.x: Since October 2023, the targeted subsidy has been ₹300 per 14.2 kg refill for up to nine refills a year. Older provisions cited ₹200 and up to 12 refills.
accepted.tq: Give priority to the latest figure while distinguishing it from the older subsidy arrangement.
accepted.sec: Clean cooking access - PM Ujjwala Yojana, refill issues

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains the refill issue faced by many PMUY households?
o: They are prohibited from obtaining LPG refills after the first connection.
They want clean fuel but face cost and habit-related barriers.
They lack any interest in clean fuel and reject LPG completely.
They are supplied only with solar cooking devices.
accepted.x: Survey findings indicate that households generally want clean fuel but face affordability and established-habit barriers to regular refilling.
accepted.tq: Select the option that captures both demand for clean fuel and the practical constraint.
accepted.sec: Clean cooking access - PM Ujjwala Yojana, refill issues

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Surya Nutan — launched by REC as a rural feeder programme
Grameen Vitrak Yojana — raised the rural share of LPG distributors from 18% to 60%
Grameen Vitrak Yojana — introduced prepaid smart meters under RDSS
Surya Nutan — provided 300 free electricity units through rooftop solar
accepted.x: Grameen Vitrak Yojana, launched in 2009, increased the rural share of LPG distributors from 18% to 60%. Surya Nutan is an indoor solar stove developed by IOCL in 2022.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched programme before rejecting swapped institutional roles.
accepted.sec: Clean cooking access - PM Ujjwala Yojana, refill issues

accepted.s: Surya Nutan, related to clean cooking access, is:
o: A feeder-separation project launched by the Ministry of Power
An indoor solar stove developed by IOCL in 2022
A rural LPG distribution programme launched in 2009
A rooftop-solar subsidy scheme launched by MNRE in 2024
accepted.x: Surya Nutan is an indoor solar stove developed by Indian Oil Corporation Limited in 2022.
accepted.tq: Use the device, developer and year together to identify the initiative.
accepted.sec: Clean cooking access - PM Ujjwala Yojana, refill issues

accepted.s: The Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS), launched in December 2014, primarily aims to strengthen:
o: Rural agricultural feeder separation and village electrification
Urban sub-transmission and distribution, metering and IT enablement
accepted.x: IPDS strengthens urban sub-transmission and distribution, metering and IT enablement.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the urban distribution focus of IPDS from the rural focus of DDUGJY.
accepted.sec: IPDS - urban distribution strengthening

accepted.s: IPDS subsumed which earlier programme?
accepted.x: The Integrated Power Development Scheme subsumed the Restructured Accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programme (R-APDRP).
accepted.tq: Identify the predecessor by separating urban and rural distribution programmes.
accepted.sec: IPDS - urban distribution strengthening

accepted.s: Which outcome has been credited to IPDS?
o: Universal LPG refilling among rural households
Electrification of all inhabited census villages
accepted.x: IPDS has been credited with improving urban power supply through strengthening urban distribution infrastructure and metering.
accepted.tq: Match the reported outcome with the scheme’s urban infrastructure function.
accepted.sec: IPDS - urban distribution strengthening
